body:
A synced folder that v0.0.111 set up is upgraded in place again, keeping every file it holds, instead of showing as `not watched (wrong_schema)`.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A synced folder that v0.0.111 set up no longer shows as `not watched (wrong_schema)` with advice to remove it and add it again. Its next `marfa folders push`, `pull`, `scan` or `watch` upgrades it in place and keeps every file, held deletes and pause it holds. Until then, `marfa folders status` and `marfa folders held` say the next sync upgrades it, and nothing needs to be removed. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** `marfa folders list` shows a paused folder from v0.0.111 as paused, not running, and a held delete in another folder still at that version gives the same advice.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.112 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 5, so v0.0.112 can restore an archive this release writes. A device's working copy store stays at version 12. If you held off upgrading from v0.0.111 because of the known issue in v0.0.112, upgrade to this release: your synced folders are upgraded in place and nothing needs to be added again.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.112...v0.0.113

On a computer with more than one synced folder, a file deleted by hand no longer sends its item to the bin when Marfa can't tell the delete from a move into another folder: the file is held until you settle it.

### Core
- **Changed:** A file missing from a synced folder after the rename grace is treated as moved only when exactly one file in another folder that Marfa read in full can be it. Its delete is sent on its own only when the computer has no other synced folder, listed or remembered, and the folder was read in full. Every other missing file, notes included, is held: no later scan, pull or unreadable pass sends its delete, and the folder's health report counts it under `held_file`. Before, a note moved into another folder that then let the file go could have its item sent to the bin. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)
- **Added:** Apps list and settle held files with `held`, `trash_held` and `keep_held` in the Swift and Node bindings. A trash that finds the file now in another readable folder keeps the item and answers that it moved.
- **Changed:** Confirming a paused removal keeps paused every file that went missing less than the rename grace ago, even when its path can't be checked, and a file that an unreadable directory of the folder might hold under another name.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa folders held <DIR>` lists the held files. `--trash <PATH>...` queues their items' deletes, after a confirmation or `--yes`; `--keep <PATH>...` keeps the items and ends the files' bindings, and `--write-back` writes the files again at once. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Changed:** `marfa folders status` shows each held file as `held` with the flag `unsure`, one line for each item when two items went missing at the same path.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.111 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 5, so v0.0.111 can restore an archive this release writes. A device's working copy store moves to version 12, and v0.0.111 can't open it afterwards.

**Known issue:** This release doesn't upgrade a synced folder that v0.0.111 set up. `marfa folders watch` shows the folder as `not watched (wrong_schema)` and advises removing it and adding it again. Don't remove it: the next release upgrades the folder in place and keeps everything. On a computer with synced folders, wait for that release before you upgrade.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.111...v0.0.112

A device can now queue an edit that is refused if the item has moved since it was read, and a synced folder shows every delete it holds and keeps a file bound to its item when Marfa refuses a state change.

### Core
- **Added:** An edit can be marked exact (`exact` on `Edit` in the Swift and Node bindings). It is sent with the version the working copy held, and if the item has moved since, the server refuses it with `version_conflict` and merges nothing: the write gets the verdict `refused`, is not sent again, and the copy shows the server's item. An exact edit on a version older than the copy already holds queues nothing and fails at once with `version_conflict`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-in-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A delete that a folder holds because Marfa can't tell where the file went, such as while another folder on the computer can't be read, is no longer shown as a delete waiting to be sent. The folder's health report counts it under `held_file`, and a file that came back and went again gets the full rename grace before its delete is sent. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-sync-status)
- **Fixed:** When Marfa refuses a folder file's state change because another device moved the item, renaming or editing the file no longer makes a second item, and a new document whose first archive is refused stays bound to the item it created. Restoring a paused removal from the bin no longer overrides a newer state set on another device. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa device items update --exact` queues an edit that the server refuses if the item has moved since the working copy read it.
- **Changed:** `marfa folders status` lists a delete held because Marfa can't tell where the file went as `held` with the flag `unsure` and its reason. A folder the computer remembers but can't reach is described as no longer listed, with advice to mount its volume.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.110 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 5, so v0.0.110 can restore an archive this release writes, and a device's working copy store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.110...v0.0.111

A move between active, archived and the bin can name the state it expects, so an undo queued offline no longer overrides a change made on another device. An item read can say who made its last state move, a folder's directories and file counts come in one request, and an app can settle a folder's unmatched and kept files.

**Breaking:** An app or `marfa device` built on this release's core works only with a server on 0.0.110 or later, and refuses an older one with `server_too_old`, because every state move a device queues now names the state it expects and an older server refuses that. Upgrade the server before the apps and command lines that keep a working copy.

### Server
- **Added:** `POST /items/{id}/transition` takes an optional `from`: `active`, `archived` or `trashed`. When the item is in another state, the server answers `409 state_conflict` with `details.expected` and `details.actual`, and nothing moves. A wrong `from` is answered before `invalid_transition`, and a transition without `from` works as before. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/errors)
- **Added:** With `include=writer`, `GET /items/{id}` and `POST /items/bulk-get` also answer `state_writer`: the sign-in that last archived, trashed or restored the item, in the shape of `writer`, or `null` where the item has not moved, a server job such as feed expiry moved it, or it moved before this release. An archive carries it and a restore keeps it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/versions)
- **Added:** `GET /folders/{id}/directories` answers one level of a folder's directories, each with the count of files directly in it and beneath it, and `under` names the directory to read. An app can draw a folder's tree without reading every `in-folder` edge.
- **Changed:** Exports and backups are archive version 5, which carries `state_writer` on each item. A restore still reads versions 1 to 5, and an instance takes one fresh backup after it upgrades.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa items transition --from <STATE>` moves an item only when it is still in the state you read. `marfa device items transition --from <STATE>` refuses with `state_conflict` and queues nothing when the working copy shows another state.
- **Added:** `marfa folders directories <id> [--under <path>]` lists a folder's directories and their file counts.
- **Changed:** After a `marfa folders unmatched --remove` that stopped part way, `marfa folders status` shows a file Marfa is unsure about as `held` with the flag `removing` and a reason, and its item is never deleted. After a `marfa folders kept --discard` that stopped, `marfa folders kept` lists the file under the private name that holds it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** A git that stalls no longer holds `marfa folders add`: the check for a directory that git tracks waits at most 1 second.

### Core
- **Changed:** Every state move a device queues names the state its copy showed. A queued move the server refuses gets the verdict `refused` with the reason `state_conflict`, and the copy shows the server's state again. Before, an Unarchive queued offline could take an item back out of the bin after another device trashed it, and bring back the items trashed with it.
- **Added:** The Swift and Node bindings take an optional `from` on `transitionItem`.
- **Added:** An app can remove a folder's unmatched files and list and discard its kept files, as `marfa folders unmatched --remove` and `marfa folders kept --discard` do, through `removeUnmatched`, `kept` and `discardKept` on `Folders` in the Swift and Node bindings. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/work-with-folder-files)
- **Added:** A device answers each item type's `origin` (`platform`, `registered`, `plugin` or `unknown`) and, for a plugin's type, the plugin's name and version, so an app can tell a plugin's type from the owner's with no server reachable. A type declaration that names `provenance` is refused as `invalid`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/items-and-types)
- **Added:** In the Swift and Node bindings, a listed folder carries `store`, the ID its copy reports under, which the server answers as `folder_store_id` in `GET /folders/{id}/status`, and an added folder says whether git tracks its directory.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types carry `state_writer` on an item, `from` on a transition, the error code `state_conflict` and the read of a folder's directories.

**Upgrading:** Upgrading changes the database and first keeps a copy, `marfa.db.before-upgrade`; v0.0.109 can't open it afterwards. Exports and backups are now archive version 5, which v0.0.109 can't restore. A device's store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.109...v0.0.110

An item read can say who wrote its current version, a saved view can be sorted by source, a device can tell when a feed item will leave the feed, and a folder no longer takes a file in from another folder on the same computer.

**Breaking:** `marfa folders pull` and `marfa folders push` no longer report the files taken in from another folder, in text or in `--json`, so a script that reads `taken` must stop reading it. In the TypeScript client's generated types, the schema `PluginInstaller` is now the shared `Writer`; code that names the old type must name `Writer`.

### Server
- **Added:** `GET /items/{id}` and `POST /items/bulk-get` take `writer` in `include`. Each answered item then carries `writer`: the `kind`, `id` and `name` of the sign-in that wrote the item's current version, as it was named then, or `null` where no sign-in wrote it. Without `include=writer` the member is absent, and a credential is told the writer only for an item whose type it may read. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/versions)
- **Added:** A saved view can sort by `source`, on create and on change, and `GET /views/{id}/items` orders items by the stored source code. An item made with no source holds the code `unknown` and sorts as that text. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/views)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa device types get <id> --json` carries the type's `feed_days`.
- **Removed:** `marfa folders pull` and `marfa folders push` no longer report the files taken in from another folder, in text or in `--json`, since a folder no longer takes one in.

### Core
- **Added:** A device answers each item type's resolved `feed_days`: the type's own feed window, or the nearest one above it that names a window, and `null` where the type names `null` or no type in its chain names one. An app can now say when a feed item will leave the feed with no server reachable. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/items-and-types)
- **Changed:** A working copy orders a view sorted by `source` as the server does.
- **Fixed:** A folder no longer takes a file in from another folder on the same computer. When an item leaves one folder's query and enters another's, the folder that now holds it writes its own file, and the folder it left keeps its file where it is, unmatched; clear the duplicate with `marfa folders unmatched --remove`. Before, the file was moved across, and if the receiving folder then dropped the item, the folder the item first left found the file gone from everywhere and sent a delete, which could put the item in the bin. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)
- **Fixed:** A file you move by hand into a folder whose query does not hold its item is kept there as unmatched, and the folder it came from writes its file again.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types carry `writer` on an item and `writer` among the values of `include`.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.108 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 4, which v0.0.108 restores, and a device's store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.108...v0.0.109

A webhook whose receiver never answers no longer piles up deliveries without end, large tables page quickly when sorted by any column, and a synced folder keeps its file when another folder on the same computer holds the item.

**Breaking:** A row cursor from a page sorted by a column (`sort=values.<column>`) that an earlier release issued is refused with `400 validation_error` naming `cursor`; list again from the start. Cursors for `id`, `updated_at` and the table's `order` keep working. `marfa folders pull --json` and `marfa folders push --json` no longer carry the `let_go` count, so a script that reads it must stop.

### Server
- **Added:** Each webhook holds at most `webhook_backlog_deliveries` pending deliveries (10,000 by default) and `webhook_backlog_bytes` bytes of pending payloads (64 MiB by default), both changed with `PATCH /config`. A delivery past either limit is recorded as `canceled` and never sent, and the deliveries already pending are kept and still sent. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/instance-settings)
- **Added:** A webhook whose every attempt has failed for 24 hours is listed in `GET /attention` and `marfa attention`, with the kind `webhook`. It leaves the list once an attempt succeeds, or the webhook is repointed, turned off or deleted. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/check-health)
- **Changed:** Redelivering a webhook delivery that would pass either limit is refused with `409 conflict` and `details.reason` `backlog_full`. The delivery stays failed, and you can redeliver it once fewer deliveries are pending. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Changed:** A table of 20,000 rows or more that is read sorted by a column now answers later pages from sort keys the server keeps, for up to 16 such columns on an instance, so a page deep in the table costs about the same as the first. The `table-row-cleanup` job fills the keys in the background, and until it has, sorted pages are still correct. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/tables)
- **Changed:** A value written as an item's ID sorts as no value in every column and for every reader, so a sort by an `item` column returns rows in `id` order.

### CLI
- **Removed:** `marfa folders pull` and `marfa folders push` no longer report files removed because another folder holds their item, in text or in `--json`, since a folder no longer removes them.

### Core
- **Changed:** A folder no longer removes a file because another folder on the same computer holds its item, which in some orders removed the last local copy. The folder the item leaves keeps the file as unmatched, and you clear the duplicate with `marfa folders unmatched --remove`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)
- **Fixed:** A file returned to a directory of a folder with several directories is read as an edit of its item, and no longer becomes a second item because another directory of the same folder has the item's file.
- **Fixed:** A file embedded in a note is attached once the `has-attachment` line that held it back resolves or is taken out; before, it stayed unattached.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types include the two webhook backlog settings, the attention kind `webhook` and the redelivery reason `backlog_full`.

**Upgrading:** Upgrading changes the database and first keeps a copy, `marfa.db.before-upgrade`; v0.0.105 can't open it afterwards. Exports and backups stay archive version 4, which v0.0.105 restores, and a device's store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.105...v0.0.108

A saved view can now group its items by whether a field is set, by status group or by source, and the admin level on the approval page that was called Limited is now Read Only, which gives only reading powers.

**Breaking:** The approval page's admin level `limited` is now `read_only`, and a post of `admin=limited` is refused with `400` and grants nothing. If you post the approval form from a script or a test, post `read_only`. Read Only no longer includes managing files (`blobs.manage`).

### Server
- **Added:** A saved view can group by `source` or `status_group`, and by whether `tags`, a property, an edge or a backref is set, with the bucket `presence`. The server refuses groupings that can't mean anything, such as a date bucket on a field that isn't a date, and names the setting it refused. This works the same through the API, the command line and the MCP tool `marfa_save_view`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/views)
- **Changed:** On the page where you approve an app or a device, the admin levels are **Full Access**, **Read Only**, **No Access** and **Custom…**. Read Only gives only server health and the activity log, and the page offers it only when it gives some, but not all, of what the app asked for. The page says what Read Only gives under the choice. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/connect-your-agent)

### CLI
- **Changed:** The help for `--group` on `marfa views create` and `marfa views update` names the new groupings.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Changed:** A view's `group.bucket` type includes `presence`.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.104 opens as it is. Exports and backups are unchanged at archive version 4, so v0.0.104 can still restore them, and a device's store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.104...v0.0.105

Marfa's own pages, for claiming, signing in, recovering a password, managing passkeys and approving an app or a device, are redrawn to one design that works on a phone, and a device sign-in now asks you to check its code before you approve it.

**Breaking:** The approval pages post a new form. Permissions are given by one admin level, posted as `admin` (`full`, `limited`, `none` or `custom`, with `powers` rows under `custom`), and a post that names a permission in `scopes` is refused with `400`. A device approval is read only after the device code was confirmed on the new check page. If you post these forms from a script or a test, post them as the pages now draw them.

### Server
- **Added:** A device sign-in now shows **Check the code** after you enter it, so you compare it with the code on your device and choose **It Matches** before the approval page opens. A link that carries someone else's device code can no longer get them a token with one click. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/connect-your-agent)
- **Added:** A public **Forgot your password?** page, at `/auth/forgot-password`, shows both ways to reset the owner's password. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/sign-in-as-the-owner)
- **Added:** When no one has claimed the server, its start log can also print a one-time setup link that works for a few minutes, beside the setup code.
- **Changed:** The sign-in, claim, recovery, passkeys and approval pages, and every notice the server shows, follow one design in light and dark, work on a phone, and no longer show the instance's name.
- **Changed:** The approval page opens with a summary of what the app gets, and **Choose…** opens the choices in place: items, profile, and one admin level (Full Access, Limited, No Access or Custom) in place of a switch for each power. If the app's access changes while the page is open, approving grants nothing and the page is drawn again with `409`.
- **Changed:** Setup and recovery codes are 25 letters and digits in five groups of five. Creating the owner's account, and choosing a new password after recovery, ask for the password twice, and the server refuses a pair that doesn't match.
- **Changed:** The sign-in page offers a passkey only when the owner has one for that address.
- **Changed:** The **Passkeys and password** page lists passkeys with **Rename…** and **Remove…**, and changing the password and signing out work without JavaScript. A wrong password on `POST /auth/confirm` or `POST /auth/owner/password` now names its field in `details.field`, so an app can tell it from an ended session; both still answer `401`.

### CLI
- **Changed:** Access words are in title case wherever the CLI shows what a key or an app holds ("Read and Edit", "Read Only", "No Access"), and the titles of rows and powers are shorter, such as "Your items" and "Make keys".

**Upgrading:** Upgrading changes the database and first keeps a copy, `marfa.db.before-upgrade`; v0.0.103 can't open it afterwards. Exports and backups are unchanged at archive version 4, so v0.0.103 can still restore them, and a device's store is unchanged.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.103...v0.0.104

Every item now has a link: one you can share or click, and one that opens the item in a Marfa app on your device.

**Breaking:** `web_url` and `app_url` are now reserved field names, so a type that declares a field with either name is refused with `400 property_shadows_field`. Rename such a field in your type definitions. A type's own `url` field, as on the built-in bookmark, file and media types, is unchanged.

### Server
- **Added:** Every item the API answers carries `web_url`, the instance's sign-in address followed by `/i/` and the item's ID, and `app_url`, `marfa://` followed by the instance's ID and the item's ID. Marfa works them out each time it answers, so `web_url` follows the sign-in address when it moves; with no sign-in address set, it uses `http://localhost` and the server's port. Both appear in lists, search results, event frames, webhook bodies and NDJSON exports. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/items)
- **Added:** Opening an item's `web_url` in a browser shows a page that hands the item to the app on your device that opens Marfa links. The page shows nothing about the item, not even whether it exists, to anyone.
- **Added:** The MCP tools that return an item or a summary of one include both links, and the MCP server tells agents to give you the item's `web_url`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa items link <id>` prints an item's `web_url`, so you can pipe it. `--app` prints `app_url`, `--json` prints both, and `--open` opens the link with your system's opener. An item in Recently Deleted still gets its link. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's `Item` and `ItemSummary` types include `web_url` and `app_url`.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.102 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 4, which v0.0.102 restores.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.102...v0.0.103

An app you approve can now add, change and remove a type's guidance, as long as you signed in to it within the last 15 minutes.

### Server
- **Added:** An app whose access holds `schema.write` can write a type's guidance through `POST /types`, `PUT /types/{id}`, `POST /plugins` and a restore when you signed in to it within the last 900 seconds. When your sign-in is older, the server answers `401 insufficient_user_authentication` with `details.max_age` 900 and writes nothing, so the app asks you to sign in again and tries once more, as it does for a restore. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/define-a-type)
- **Added:** The MCP tool `marfa_save_type` takes guidance from an app the same way. When your sign-in is too old, the tool answers `insufficient_user_authentication`, and the connection asks you to sign in again the next time it authorizes.
- **Changed:** Installing or upgrading a plugin now judges guidance type by type against what is stored. A key an app made, which still can't change guidance, can now upgrade a plugin whose types keep the guidance already stored; before, any plugin with guidance was refused for it.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types include the `401` answer on `POST /types`, `PUT /types/{id}` and `POST /plugins`.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.101 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 4, which v0.0.101 restores.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.101...v0.0.102

A connector can now move its items back from a type you mapped one of its kinds onto before, so changing a mapping no longer strands them.

### Server
- **Added:** Each entry in `rewrites` from `GET /plugins/{name}/connector/mapping` names `from`: for each kind, the types the rewrite moves the connector's items from. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)
- **Changed:** Exports and backups are now archive version 4. They carry each connector's former mapped types and its open rewrite requests, so a rewrite on a restored instance still moves every item back. A restore still reads a version 3 archive. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/export-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** When you map a connector's kind onto a type, rewrite its items there, then map the kind back to its own type or onto another type, a new rewrite now moves the connector's items off the type the kind left. Before, the connector could not reach those items, and every later write for them was refused `type_not_permitted`. While the rewrite is open, the connector can list, read and move only its own items there, never yours or another source's, and its reach ends when it clears the request. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)

### CLI
- **Fixed:** `marfa plugins mapping rewrite --dry-run` counts the items a rewrite would move, and says "would move N onto TYPE". Before, it counted the items already on the target, which a rewrite never moves. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types include `from` on a connector mapping's rewrite requests.

**Upgrading:** Upgrading changes the database and first keeps a copy, `marfa.db.before-upgrade`; v0.0.100 can't open it afterwards. Exports and backups are now archive version 4, which v0.0.100 can't restore.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.100...v0.0.101

A filter that compares a list with a number or a boolean now matches the list's members, and built-in edge type labels are now in title case.

### Server
- **Changed:** Built-in edge type labels and reverse labels capitalize every word, as field labels do: `GET /edge-types` now returns `In Collection`, `Derived From` and `Subject Of` where it returned `In collection`, `Derived from` and `Subject of`. An app that matches on a label's text should match the new spelling, or better, on the edge type's `id`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/edges)
- **Fixed:** A filter that compares a property holding a list with a number or a boolean now tests the list's members, not the list's text. `properties.words eq 5` selects an item whose list holds `5`, `contains 5` selects the same items and no longer matches `[15]`, and `neq 5` selects a list that holds no `5`. A range such as `gt 4` still selects no list. Saved views that use such a filter may now list different items. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/list-filter-search)

### CLI
- **Changed:** The help for `marfa update start` and `marfa server upgrade` now says that a release opens the database of any earlier release from 0.0.86 on, except one 0.0.88 wrote, and upgrades it in place, keeping a copy first as `marfa.db.before-upgrade`.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A device's working copy answers a filter on a list with a number or a boolean the same way the server does.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.99 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay at archive version 3, so v0.0.99 can restore an archive this release writes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.99...v0.0.100

A connector can now sync onto the type you map its kind to, such as a tracker's issues onto your own tickets, and a plugin can say where its connector's code is.

### Server
- **Added:** A plugin's `connector` section can carry `code`: the `https` address of the connector's code file, its SHA-256 and its size. The owner now signs in with a username, telemetry is set from any app with no restart and now includes metrics, an agent at `/mcp/admin` can purge the trash and remove connectors with a confirmation, and a device keeps the work a server restored from a backup lost.

**Breaking:** The owner claims and signs in with a username, not an email: a client that sends `email` to claim or sign in is refused, and the email is now an optional profile field. The server no longer reads the `OTEL_*` variables, `MARFA_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` or `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`: after you upgrade, set the `otel_` stored settings and `telemetry_enabled` with `marfa config update --file -`. The `error_webhook_url` setting is gone: to hear of faults, follow `attention.raised` with a webhook. A type that sets `enum_values` on a field or column that is not an `enum` is refused with `400 invalid_schema`. The command line no longer reads `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` or `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`.

### Server
- **Added:** An agent connected at `/mcp/admin` can purge chosen items or a page of the trash, delete a connector, clear a connector's state and retire an inbound endpoint. Each act shows a preview first and runs only with a single-use confirmation, and it changes nothing if what it would remove changed in the meantime. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Added:** A new instance can be claimed in the sign-in page that an AI client opens when it connects, and the person then lands on that client's approval page already signed in. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/claude-and-chatgpt)
- **Added:** The server exports request duration and memory use as OpenTelemetry metrics, to `otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_endpoint` or `v1/metrics` under the base endpoint. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Added:** The server lists its own faults in what needs the owner's attention and announces each new one at once as `attention.raised`, even when the database cannot be written. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Added:** A tag replace at `PUT /items/{id}/tags` can name the tags the client read in `read_tags`, and is refused with `409 version_conflict` when another writer changed them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-safely)
- **Changed:** The owner signs in with a username, and can change it later at `PATCH /profile` without losing passkeys, sessions, keys or app access. Apps read it through the new `username` profile permission. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/sign-in-as-the-owner)
- **Changed:** The OpenTelemetry settings are stored settings that any app or key with `config.manage` can change, and a change takes effect with no restart. `telemetry_enabled` pauses all telemetry without clearing secrets. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Changed:** A sign-in counts as recent for 15 minutes instead of 5.
- **Changed:** `/mcp/admin` advertises every permission its tools need, so a client approved with full access sees every admin tool. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** An update downloads only from Marfa's release address on GitHub, starts only for a credential that still holds `instance.maintain`, puts the old release back when the new one fails to start, and reports an update that did not finish instead of calling it `succeeded`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade)
- **Changed:** An app the owner signed in to can widen a key with `keys.mint`, and make a key that outlives the app's own access with `owner_key`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-keys)
- **Fixed:** An object store that `allow_private_addresses` now refuses is reported as unusable in `/health`, `/attention` and `/blobs/stores`, and nothing is purged while it is refused. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** When a file's bytes change, what was read from the old bytes (its text, size and length) is cleared so that it is read again.
- **Fixed:** An item's preview and a name taken from its body read as a reader reads the text, without front matter, footnotes, highlight markers or table pipes.
- **Fixed:** A server keeps sole use of its database, blob folder and backup folder even when someone removes its `.server-lock` file, so a second server can no longer start on the same folder.
- **Fixed:** A Linux user install no longer fails to start because the server made its `data` folder writable by other accounts.
- **Removed:** The `error_webhook_url` setting.

### CLI
- **Changed:** `marfa setup claim` takes `--username`, with `--email` optional, and `marfa profile update` takes `--username`, `--email` and `--clear-email`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Changed:** The `marfa folders` commands say what happened in plain words, `folders add --folder` takes a folder's title as well as its ID, and `folders inventory` shows each folder's title. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/sync-a-folder)
- **Changed:** Messages name apps and actors, give the request ID to quote, print a failed start's log line by line, and say when a store is read only.
- **Removed:** PostHog events from the command line. It still exports OTLP traces through the standard `OTEL_*` variables. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/client-telemetry)

### Core
- **Added:** When a server is restored to an earlier point, a device keeps the items, edges, tags, deletions and table rows the server lost, and queues them back blocked `server_restored` until the person releases or withdraws them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Added:** A folder can narrow beneath a project that is one of its own files, from the first sync. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)
- **Fixed:** A folder replaces or removes a file only after proving it is the file it read, so a save an editor makes in the meantime is kept, and reported as `kept`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** When two directories on one computer follow the same folder and its query narrows, each keeps its own file of an item the query left out.
- **Fixed:** An edit read from a new item before its create was taken is no longer refused `invalid` once the create is taken. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-in-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A tag replace over tags another writer changed is blocked as a conflict, and the copy keeps what the person wrote.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Fixed:** `@withmarfa/client` loads through `require` as well as `import`, so a CommonJS project such as a Raycast extension can use it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/typescript-script)

The server's PostHog error tracking is now two stored settings you can change from any app with no restart, a device copy renews its sign-in instead of signing a person out when a long read outlasts its token, and queued writes and stores opened by a path are kept safer.

**Breaking:** The server no longer reads `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` or `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`. If you send your server's faults to PostHog, set `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token` together after you upgrade, with `marfa config update --file -`. A self-hosted PostHog must serve the capture v1 endpoint. On a Mac, a working copy opened by a plain path on an NFS, SMB, AFP or WebDAV volume is now refused: keep the store on a local disk.

### Server
- **Added:** The stored settings `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token` send a report of each server fault to PostHog's error tracking. They are set together, take effect from the next fault, are never shown back, and a host on a private address needs `allow_private_addresses`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Changed:** `error_reporting_enabled` can be on only when `error_webhook_url` or the PostHog pair is set. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/settings)
- **Changed:** Traces, log records and fault reports carry the server's release as `service.version`, and the server no longer calls itself `production` unless `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` says so. A fault report names its trace when traces are exported.
- **Changed:** A health check or a quick read that went well is no longer exported as an OTLP log record. Its line in the request log on standard output stays.
- **Removed:** The `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` and `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` environment variables, for the server. The command line still reads them.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A catch-up or a hydration whose sign-in token expires while it reads the event stream renews the sign-in and reads on from the last event it took. Before, it ended `stream_incomplete` with `credential_ended`, and a Swift app signed the person out. A copy that holds a key, or a sign-in that has ended, still ends the call. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A queued write is synced to the store's log on every commit, so it survives the app or the system stopping. On a Mac, a sudden power cut can still lose the last writes the drive had not stored, and the store stays whole. Writes and hydration take a little longer. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A store opened through a symbolic link keeps its lock, its file bytes and any set-aside copy beside the file the link leads to, so an upload queued through one name is no longer lost through the other.
- **Changed:** A store opened by a plain path is refused on a file system that does not lock files, or where SQLite cannot use write-ahead mode, instead of risking two writers. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A read that is stopped starts no further request or sign-in renewal.

### Swift SDK
- **Fixed:** A long hydration or catch-up no longer signs a person out when the access token expires mid-read, once the Swift package moves to this release.

An agent at `/mcp/admin` can now do the owner tasks its permissions open, signing out ends an app's access even after a renewal, and working copies and synced folders keep people's data safer when the server, the credential or the folder changes underneath them.

**Breaking:** With `object_store_path_style` set to `false`, an object store endpoint whose host ends in more than one dot, or has an empty label or a label longer than 63 characters, is now refused with `400` at `/config`, and a stored one attaches no store. Before you upgrade, check `object_store_endpoint` and write the host with at most one dot at its end.

### Server
- **Added:** An agent connected at `/mcp/admin` can read the owner's state and make the owner's guarded changes that its credential's permissions open: settings, the trash, apps, backups, maintenance, connectors, files and sign-ins, with the same rules and refusals as the API. Destructive acts, such as emptying the trash or revoking an app, are not offered. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** A webhook delivery checks that its key still stands after connecting to the receiver and before sending, and sends nothing when it no longer does. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Fixed:** Revoking an app's refresh token at `POST /oauth/revoke` ends the app's grant whenever the token has not ended or expired, even if a later renewal already replaced it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)
- **Fixed:** `GET /health` reports `blob_storage` as `down` when the blob folder belongs to another store, and a `blob-orphans` run counts a blob as purged once its record is gone.
- **Fixed:** An object store host with several dots at its end is counted at its true length against the 253-character limit.

### CLI
- **Fixed:** `marfa folders confirm` scans the folder again before it lets go of a paused removal. A file that came back under another name keeps its item, and a file it cannot check is reported in `unsure` and never moved to the bin. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)

### Core
- **Fixed:** A working copy confirms that the server at its address is still its own instance before it sends item IDs, file hashes or names, and again after a credential renewal. When another instance answers, it sends nothing more and ends `copy_expired` with the reason `instance_changed`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A write whose answer was lost is read back before it is sent again under a different credential, so an edit is no longer applied twice and a delete that landed is no longer shown as refused. A removal or a create the read cannot settle safely stays queued instead of being sent. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A synced folder's quick check walks the folder where no change event can arrive, such as a directory the system will not watch or a file with another hard link, so those changes are no longer missed until the next full pass.

### Swift SDK
- **Fixed:** A crash inside the core during a call reaches the app as `MarfaError.fault`, instead of an error the app could not match or as `store`, once the Swift package moves to this release. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/swift-sdk/errors-and-testing)

Object stores addressed by virtual host now work, changing where files and backups go asks for a recent sign-in, and narrowing an app also ends the keys it made that hold more.

**Breaking:** Changing `backup_path` or any `object_store_` setting now needs a sign-in from the last five minutes: an API key is refused with `403 app_sign_in_required`, so use `marfa config set` on the machine where the server runs, or an app after a fresh sign-in. With `object_store_path_style` set to `false`, set `object_store_endpoint` to the store's bare host, without the bucket. An `object_store_region` or `object_store_bucket` that is not a valid name is now refused with `400 validation_error`.

### Server
- **Changed:** Changing `backup_path`, `object_store_bucket`, `object_store_endpoint`, `object_store_region`, `object_store_path_style` or `object_store_prefix` needs a recent sign-in, and changing the bucket or the endpoint removes the stored secret access key unless the same change sets one. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Changed:** Narrowing an app's access also revokes every key the app made that reaches beyond the new access, and the answer to `PATCH /grants/{id}` says how many in `revoked_keys`. Keys within the new access keep working. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)
- **Changed:** A restore that would add a setting the instance does not have yet also needs `config.manage`. Without it, the restore is refused with `403` before anything is written, naming the permission and the settings. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Changed:** `object_store_region` and `object_store_bucket` must be valid names, and a write outside the rule is refused with `400 validation_error` naming the setting.
- **Fixed:** An object store with `object_store_path_style` set to `false` is reached at the bucket's own host, `<bucket>.<endpoint host>`, for every request and signed link. Before, the bucket was left out of the address and such a store never worked. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** A stored object store setting that cannot be used no longer stops the server from starting. The server attaches no store, serves files from its disk and names the setting on the attention list until you correct it, with no restart.

### CLI
- **Changed:** `marfa apps narrow` says how many keys it revoked that the app made. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)

### Core
- **Added:** A renewal that an app's credential renewer fails ends with its own error, `renewal_refused`, with a reason an app can word, instead of `invalid`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Changed:** Pushing a folder, and the quick check after you edit a file in a large synced folder, do much less work, so changes reach the server sooner.
- **Fixed:** Opening a working copy on a full disk answers `storage_full` instead of `store`, and a store that a newer build made is refused with `wrong_schema` and left exactly as it was. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** On a volume that keeps names apart by case, such as most Linux file systems, a file held beside a note in another case (`Q.md` beside `q.md`) no longer replaces the note's file after the note is moved or retitled. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/work-with-folder-files)
- **Fixed:** Stopping a sync ends it at once, instead of waiting up to 30 seconds for a request the sync had already started.
